key_insight: Crystal VAE atom-wise latent representations naturally separate by elemental family, enabling FamilySpace to steer generated crystals toward user-specified family compositions.
engineering_relevance: Family-level composition control can guide materials discovery toward promising chemical regions without additional optimization methods such as reinforcement learning.
method: Identify elemental-family regions in the crystal VAE latent space.
Train a flow model with distinct family-indexed source components and family-matched source–target pairs.
Use a user-defined family template to select the source component for each atom during generation.
evidence_signal: On MP-20 and MPTS-52, FamilySpace reports competitive generation performance and prescribed family-composition matching; selected templates increase the fraction of crystals predicted stable or metastable.
watch_item: Predicted stability does not establish experimental synthesizability, and family-level control does not specify exact elemental identities.
paper_title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation
